pr_comments: Is there some better way to handle that call to `async_delete_issue()`? It is now called every time a request was successful.

**edit**
Wait, I see. You mean something like what is implemented with `async_create_fix_flow()`?
The `demo` integration has a smaller example of this (it shows the possible ways an repairs issue can work)
Hmm good one, we currently have no ability to pass data into an issue. @emontnemery Is that something we should consider?
@DCSBL, @frenck format the `issue_id` to include the config entry id, then use that to access `hass.data[DOMAIN][entry_id]`
This allows storing data in issues: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/76288

Thanks @emontnemery! I've tried to implement this. I had some mypy issues that told me that `data` was an optional and stuff. I've worked around this a bit, I think it can be better but I have no idea how at this moment

issue_context.title: Not being notified about HomeWizard Energy having problem with disabled API
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I'm using HomeWizard Energy integration to add my HomeWizard P1 Meter to the HomeAssistant. It was working fine for a few months, but while adding another unrelated integration today, I noticed that the HomeWizard Energy integration has a red warning about "API is disabled and needs to be enabled in the app". Apparently, the toggle to share the data with local API was disabled for some reason on the HomeWizard Energy app (maybe because of their updates) and I haven't noticed this for more than a week, so the data hasn't been transferred to the HomeAssistant for this period.
Shouldn't this type of warning also appear as a notification in HomeAssistant, so I can take some actions as soon as possible and not lose any significant data for this simple reason?

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2022.7.3

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

HomeWizard Energy

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/homewizard

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_
comments:
Hey there @dcsbl, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`homewizard`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L464) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

Hey! That should not happen, there is no update that should disable or block the API (and we have absolutely no intention to do so 😉)

~Please contact HomeWizard support via homewizard.com (click the chat icon in the bottom right. You can send a link to this issue. If they can't solve it and/or you think it is related to this integration, then please let us know here!~

Sorry I've read too quickly.

> Shouldn't this type of warning also appear as a notification in HomeAssistant, so I can take some actions as soon as possible and not lose any significant data for this simple reason?

It is put as warning in the log and the integration tells the device is 'unavailable'. I don't know if there are other integrations that add a notification when the API stops or so. I think that is up to the core team if we should add that.

On the other hand; I am pretty sure the 'Enable API' toggle is not changed by HomeWizard (intentionally or accidentally). I think you, or a user with your account did that by accident. In that case, should Home Assistant be the one that sends out a notification or the HomeWizard Energy app?

Thanks for the quick reply.
I'm almost sure that I haven't disabled the Local API on the app, and no one else has access to do so, but I will keep an eye on it and will report it here if it ever happens again.
As you mentioned, the important point here is to get notified when such a thing happens. I believe it should be the Home Assistant that sends out a notification since it's the Home Assistant that is losing the historical data in this case.
And as a side note, I wish there was a way to sync the historical data in such a case, so the user wouldn't miss any data on Home Assistant.

> As you mentioned, the important point here is to get notified when such a thing happens. I believe it should be the Home Assistant that sends out a notification since it's the Home Assistant that is losing the historical data in this case.

I can implement this, but it is up to the core team to decide if an integration should do that.. @frenck ?

> And as a side note, I wish there was a way to sync the historical data in such a case, so the user wouldn't miss any data on Home Assistant.

Would be nice! Bit as far as I know it is not possible to do that with Home Assistant. The data is also not available in the P1 meter as it only knows the real-time data.
@DCSBL Can this kind of notification appear in the new "[repairs](https://www.home-assistant.io/blog/2022/08/03/release-20228/#introducing-repairs-you-can-fix-it)" section now?
Nice, yes! Will take a look into that 👍. I think that is the right place.
This repair stuff is quite cool and I think it is really helpful to solve an issue like this one. A PR is opened to add a repair entry when API is disabled.

There hasn't been any activity on this issue recently. Due to the high number of incoming GitHub notifications, we have to clean some of the old issues, as many of them have already been resolved with the latest updates.
Please make sure to update to the latest Home Assistant version and check if that solves the issue. Let us know if that works for you by adding a comment 👍
This issue has now been marked as stale and will be closed if no further activity occurs. Thank you for your contributions.
